policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word order only: both readings contain the same words (proseche_in he_mas), and English 'we ought to give the more earnest heed' cannot register Greek constituent order. No ASV note maps here.

ASV prints the longer text: 'And didst set him over the works of thy hands' renders kai kateste_sas auton epi ta erga to_n cheiro_n sou, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many authorities omit And didst . . . hands' confirms the translators had the clause in their text and relegated its absence to the margin.
Word order only: to_ gar vs gar to_. 'For in that he subjected' reflects both alike, and no ASV note maps here.

ASV 'in that he subjected all things unto him' has an unitalicized dative object 'unto him' answering auto_; the shorter reading leaves it unexpressed, so the English wording distinguishes the longer text.

ASV 'that by the grace of God he should taste of death' renders chariti theou; cho_ris theou would read 'apart from God', which the ASV does not print even in the margin (its only note here is an alternative_rendering on 'a little lower').

The ASV's mapped gloss 'Greek blood and flesh' reports the order of the text the translators rendered, which is haimatos kai sarkos; the English 'flesh and blood' is the idiomatic inversion the note exists to flag, so the note, not the English, settles the unit.
